# Reco Raises $55 Million for Agentic Security

The company will use the funds to expand its sales, partnerships, channels, and customer support teams.

By

Ionut Arghire

|

 + Flipboard + Reddit + Whatsapp + Whatsapp + Email

Cybersecurity funding

Agentic cybersecurity firm Reco today announced raising $55 million in a strategic funding round that brings the total raised by the company to $140 million. [...] The investment round was led by AT&T Ventures, with additional support from new investors Forestay and Quadrille Capital.

Founded in 2020, New York-based Reco provides organizations with an overview of the agents that are active in their environments and the risks they pose.

The company shows security teams which identities the AI agents use, their permissions, what data and which systems they reach, and the workflows they can initiate.

results.title: Reco Raises $55 Million to Help Companies Secure AI Agents | Межа
results.content:
Reco raised $55 million in a financing round that extended its $30 million Series B, announced in February. Investors include customer AT&T, through its venture arm, as well as Forestay and Quadrille Capital. The startup has raised $140 million in total.

Klein said Reco’s valuation more than doubled after the previous round was announced. He did not disclose the company’s exact valuation. [...] Reco’s round comes amid growth in the AI agent security market: companies are increasingly adopting these systems, while startups compete to help businesses detect agents and control their access and actions.

Related news for you:

 Autonomous AI agents accessed real systems during security tests, exposing risks linked to internet access, stolen credentials, weak isolation, and excessive permissions.

The company plans to triple that figure. Its platform supports more than 280 applications, and the new funding will go toward hiring, sales, partnerships, and customer support.

results.title: Reco raises USD $55 million with AT&T Ventures backing
results.content:
Reco has raised an additional USD $55 million, with participation from AT&T Ventures, bringing the security software company's total funding to USD $140 million.

The round also includes backing from Forestay and Quadrille Capital. Reco will use the funding to expand sales, partnerships, channels and customer support as large companies broaden their use of AI agents across internal systems and business applications. [...] Reco's latest funding round underlines how quickly governance and oversight tools are becoming part of enterprise AI spending as companies move from limited trials to broader deployment of agents across their operations.
